Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents#442 merge SHA (PR-owned
    # lifecycle: test once per state, silent updates, pre-merge validation).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

This is a tiny PR: changes `contents: read` → `contents: write` in machine-sm.yml. This is a security-relevant change (elevating workflow token permissions). Let me review:

Context: The workflow runs on schedule (cron every 10 min) and workflow_dispatch. It calls a reusable workflow from a third-party repo `IstiN/dmtools-agents` pinned to a SHA. Granting `contents: write` to a workflow that runs on schedule means the GITHUB_TOKEN with write access is available to the called reusable workflow... Actually, in a reusable workflow call, the called workflow inherits permissions from the caller's GITHUB_TOKEN but capped at the caller's. The called workflow is pinned to a SHA (good — immutable pin). The secrets block explicitly maps SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN.

Security considerations:
1. `contents: write` on a cron-triggered workflow — this is necessary per the PR rationale: the factory does `updatePullRequestBranch` which pushes a merge commit onto the PR head branch using the workflow token. GitHub requires contents:write for that at refs level. This is a known GitHub behavior — updating a PR branch via API requires contents:write. Actually the `updatePullRequestBranch` REST API endpoint requires "Contents" write permission. So the claim is accurate.
2. Trigger surface: schedule + workflow_dispatch only. No pull_request_target, no issue_comment, no untrusted input execution. So the write token is not exposed to untrusted PR code directly in this caller. But the called workflow checks out code? The factory "engine checkout" — it checks out the engine (dmtools-agents) and runs rules. Does it check out PR code? "pre-merge validation" might check out PR branches. If the called workflow (third-party, even if pinned) checks out and executes PR code with contents:write token, that's a risk — but that's the factory's design, pinned SHA, and the same author owns both repos (IstiN). 

3. The comment block says "the org default caps the token at read-only" — so this explicit block is needed.

Findings:
- The permission escalation is justified and the rationale is well documented inline.
- One consideration: principle of least privilege — could scope contents:write only to the job that needs it. Here there's only one job (the reusable call), so top-level is fine.
- Since the called workflow is from a different repo (IstiN/dmtools-agents — same owner though), permissions of the called workflow cannot exceed the caller's. Granting contents:write here raises the ceiling for the callee. The callee is pinned to a SHA which mitigates supply-chain mutation.
- Potential concern: `actions: write` + `contents: write` + cron every 10 min — broad standing token. But each permission has a documented use.
- Is there a risk that a PR from a fork could trigger this? No — schedule and workflow_dispatch only run on the default branch context.

Check AGENTS.md for conventions. Also check whether there are tests guarding workflow files (e.g., test that checks permissions?). Let me grep for machine-sm in tests.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap

        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string

# NO permissions block here: the factory's jobs declare their own write
# scopes, and a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the caller —
# an explicit read-only block here made every call fail validation with
# startup_failure (live bisect, 2026-09-18). The repository default

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)

              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)

              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents#442 merge SHA (PR-owned
    # lifecycle: test once per state, silent updates, pre-merge validation).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

This is a tiny PR: changes `contents: read` → `contents: write` in machine-sm.yml. This is a security-relevant change (elevating workflow token permissions). Let me review:

Context: The workflow runs on schedule (cron every 10 min) and workflow_dispatch. It calls a reusable workflow from a third-party repo `IstiN/dmtools-agents` pinned to a SHA. Granting `contents: write` to a workflow that runs on schedule means the GITHUB_TOKEN with write access is available to the called reusable workflow... Actually, in a reusable workflow call, the called workflow inherits permissions from the caller's GITHUB_TOKEN but capped at the caller's. The called workflow is pinned to a SHA (good — immutable pin). The secrets block explicitly maps SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN.

Security considerations:
1. `contents: write` on a cron-triggered workflow — this is necessary per the PR rationale: the factory does `updatePullRequestBranch` which pushes a merge commit onto the PR head branch using the workflow token. GitHub requires contents:write for that at refs level. This is a known GitHub behavior — updating a PR branch via API requires contents:write. Actually the `updatePullRequestBranch` REST API endpoint requires "Contents" write permission. So the claim is accurate.
2. Trigger surface: schedule + workflow_dispatch only. No pull_request_target, no issue_comment, no untrusted input execution. So the write token is not exposed to untrusted PR code directly in this caller. But the called workflow checks out code? The factory "engine checkout" — it checks out the engine (dmtools-agents) and runs rules. Does it check out PR code? "pre-merge validation" might check out PR branches. If the called workflow (third-party, even if pinned) checks out and executes PR code with contents:write token, that's a risk — but that's the factory's design, pinned SHA, and the same author owns both repos (IstiN). 

3. The comment block says "the org default caps the token at read-only" — so this explicit block is needed.

Findings:
- The permission escalation is justified and the rationale is well documented inline.
- One consideration: principle of least privilege — could scope contents:write only to the job that needs it. Here there's only one job (the reusable call), so top-level is fine.
- Since the called workflow is from a different repo (IstiN/dmtools-agents — same owner though), permissions of the called workflow cannot exceed the caller's. Granting contents:write here raises the ceiling for the callee. The callee is pinned to a SHA which mitigates supply-chain mutation.
- Potential concern: `actions: write` + `contents: write` + cron every 10 min — broad standing token. But each permission has a documented use.
- Is there a risk that a PR from a fork could trigger this? No — schedule and workflow_dispatch only run on the default branch context.

Check AGENTS.md for conventions. Also check whether there are tests guarding workflow files (e.g., test that checks permissions?). Let me grep for machine-sm in tests.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in

              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

Context: The workflow runs on schedule (cron every 10 min) and workflow_dispatch. It calls a reusable workflow from a third-party repo `IstiN/dmtools-agents` pinned to a SHA. Granting `contents: write` to a workflow that runs on schedule means the GITHUB_TOKEN with write access is available to the called reusable workflow... Actually, in a reusable workflow call, the called workflow inherits permissions from the caller's GITHUB_TOKEN but capped at the caller's. The called workflow is pinned to a SHA (good — immutable pin). The secrets block explicitly maps SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN.

Security considerations:
1. `contents: write` on a cron-triggered workflow — this is necessary per the PR rationale: the factory does `updatePullRequestBranch` which pushes a merge commit onto the PR head branch using the workflow token. GitHub requires contents:write for that at refs level. This is a known GitHub behavior — updating a PR branch via API requires contents:write. Actually the `updatePullRequestBranch` REST API endpoint requires "Contents" write permission. So the claim is accurate.
2. Trigger surface: schedule + workflow_dispatch only. No pull_request_target, no issue_comment, no untrusted input execution. So the write token is not exposed to untrusted PR code directly in this caller. But the called workflow checks out code? The factory "engine checkout" — it checks out the engine (dmtools-agents) and runs rules. Does it check out PR code? "pre-merge validation" might check out PR branches. If the called workflow (third-party, even if pinned) checks out and executes PR code with contents:write token, that's a risk — but that's the factory's design, pinned SHA, and the same author owns both repos (IstiN). 

3. The comment block says "the org default caps the token at read-only" — so this explicit block is needed.

Findings:
- The permission escalation is justified and the rationale is well documented inline.
- One consideration: principle of least privilege — could scope contents:write only to the job that needs it. Here there's only one job (the reusable call), so top-level is fine.
- Since the called workflow is from a different repo (IstiN/dmtools-agents — same owner though), permissions of the called workflow cannot exceed the caller's. Granting contents:write here raises the ceiling for the callee. The callee is pinned to a SHA which mitigates supply-chain mutation.
- Potential concern: `actions: write` + `contents: write` + cron every 10 min — broad standing token. But each permission has a documented use.
- Is there a risk that a PR from a fork could trigger this? No — schedule and workflow_dispatch only run on the default branch context.

  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,

  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only

  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).

# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents#442 merge SHA (PR-owned
    # lifecycle: test once per state, silent updates, pre-merge validation).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

This is a tiny PR: changes `contents: read` → `contents: write` in machine-sm.yml. This is a security-relevant change (elevating workflow token permissions). Let me review:

Context: The workflow runs on schedule (cron every 10 min) and workflow_dispatch. It calls a reusable workflow from a third-party repo `IstiN/dmtools-agents` pinned to a SHA. Granting `contents: write` to a workflow that runs on schedule means the GITHUB_TOKEN with write access is available to the called reusable workflow... Actually, in a reusable workflow call, the called workflow inherits permissions from the caller's GITHUB_TOKEN but capped at the caller's. The called workflow is pinned to a SHA (good — immutable pin). The secrets block explicitly maps SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN.

Security considerations:
1. `contents: write` on a cron-triggered workflow — this is necessary per the PR rationale: the factory does `updatePullRequestBranch` which pushes a merge commit onto the PR head branch using the workflow token. GitHub requires contents:write for that at refs level. This is a known GitHub behavior — updating a PR branch via API requires contents:write. Actually the `updatePullRequestBranch` REST API endpoint requires "Contents" write permission. So the claim is accurate.
2. Trigger surface: schedule + workflow_dispatch only. No pull_request_target, no issue_comment, no untrusted input execution. So the write token is not exposed to untrusted PR code directly in this caller. But the called workflow checks out code? The factory "engine checkout" — it checks out the engine (dmtools-agents) and runs rules. Does it check out PR code? "pre-merge validation" might check out PR branches. If the called workflow (third-party, even if pinned) checks out and executes PR code with contents:write token, that's a risk — but that's the factory's design, pinned SHA, and the same author owns both repos (IstiN). 

3. The comment block says "the org default caps the token at read-only" — so this explicit block is needed.

Findings:
- The permission escalation is justified and the rationale is well documented inline.
- One consideration: principle of least privilege — could scope contents:write only to the job that needs it. Here there's only one job (the reusable call), so top-level is fine.
- Since the called workflow is from a different repo (IstiN/dmtools-agents — same owner though), permissions of the called workflow cannot exceed the caller's. Granting contents:write here raises the ceiling for the callee. The callee is pinned to a SHA which mitigates supply-chain mutation.
- Potential concern: `actions: write` + `contents: write` + cron every 10 min — broad standing token. But each permission has a documented use.
- Is there a risk that a PR from a fork could trigger this? No — schedule and workflow_dispatch only run on the default branch context.

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

Now I have full context. Assessment of the PR:

The change: `contents: read` → `contents: write` on machine-sm.yml.

Security analysis:
1. Justification is accurate: the `updatePullRequestBranch` REST API (used by `gh api .../update-branch` or the "Update branch" button) requires Contents:write permission. Documented GitHub behavior. ✓
2. Trigger surface: only `schedule` (cron, runs on default branch) and `workflow_dispatch`. No `pull_request_target`, no `issues`/`issue_comment` trigger. The write token is not directly exposed to untrusted PR/fork code via triggers. ✓
3. The called reusable workflow is pinned to an immutable SHA (guarded by test). ✓
4. Least privilege: single job (the reusable call) — top-level permissions block is the only place to grant; can't scope finer. Note: GitHub reusable workflows: the called workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN permissions can't exceed caller's; explicit block is required since org default is read-only.
5. Risk: contents:write + pull-requests:write + actions:write token handed to a third-party reusable workflow (IstiN/dmtools-agents — same owner as this repo, so first-party effectively). Combined with a standing cron every 10 min, this is a broad standing write token. Mitigated by SHA pin + same-owner. Worth an informational note: any future factory update (bumping the SHA) now runs with contents:write — the pin test guards the bump, but reviewers must re-review the factory at the new SHA since it gains write scope. This is a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? I'd say SUGGESTION (process note).
6. Consistency: ai-teammate.yml comment says "The repository default (Settings → Actions → Workflow permissions: read and write) governs" while machine-sm.yml's comment says "the org default caps the token at read-only". These are contradictory claims about the repo/org default. Minor inconsistency — SUGGESTION. Actually the machine-sm comment about the org default was pre-existing context comment; the new comment is fine. The ai-teammate claim vs machine-sm claim differ. This could mislead. It's on unchanged lines in ai-teammate.yml though — outside diff, so it goes in general comment.
7. One subtlety: with `contents: write`, the silent-token input `silent-token: ${{ github.token }}` now carries a write token into the factory as an INPUT. # Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents#442 merge SHA (PR-owned
    # lifecycle: test once per state, silent updates, pre-merge validation).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 5519dc759a6108dc46e96f1e9903bf8b6eb36991
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

This is a tiny PR: changes `contents: read` → `contents: write` in machine-sm.yml. This is a security-relevant change (elevating workflow token permissions). Let me review:

Context: The workflow runs on schedule (cron every 10 min) and workflow_dispatch. It calls a reusable workflow from a third-party repo `IstiN/dmtools-agents` pinned to a SHA. Granting `contents: write` to a workflow that runs on schedule means the GITHUB_TOKEN with write access is available to the called reusable workflow... Actually, in a reusable workflow call, the called workflow inherits permissions from the caller's GITHUB_TOKEN but capped at the caller's. The called workflow is pinned to a SHA (good — immutable pin). The secrets block explicitly maps SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN.

Security considerations:
1. `contents: write` on a cron-triggered workflow — this is necessary per the PR rationale: the factory does `updatePullRequestBranch` which pushes a merge commit onto the PR head branch using the workflow token. GitHub requires contents:write for that at refs level. This is a known GitHub behavior — updating a PR branch via API requires contents:write. Actually the `updatePullRequestBranch` REST API endpoint requires "Contents" write permission. So the claim is accurate.
2. Trigger surface: schedule + workflow_dispatch only. No pull_request_target, no issue_comment, no untrusted input execution. So the write token is not exposed to untrusted PR code directly in this caller. But the called workflow checks out code? The factory "engine checkout" — it checks out the engine (dmtools-agents) and runs rules. Does it check out PR code? "pre-merge validation" might check out PR branches. If the called workflow (third-party, even if pinned) checks out and executes PR code with contents:write token, that's a risk — but that's the factory's design, pinned SHA, and the same author owns both repos (IstiN). 

3. The comment block says "the org default caps the token at read-only" — so this explicit block is needed.

Findings:
- The permission escalation is justified and the rationale is well documented inline.
- One consideration: principle of least privilege — could scope contents:write only to the job that needs it. Here there's only one job (the reusable call), so top-level is fine.
- Since the called workflow is from a different repo (IstiN/dmtools-agents — same owner though), permissions of the called workflow cannot exceed the caller's. Granting contents:write here raises the ceiling for the callee. The callee is pinned to a SHA which mitigates supply-chain mutation.
- Potential concern: `actions: write` + `contents: write` + cron every 10 min — broad standing token. But each permission has a documented use.
- Is there a risk that a PR from a fork could trigger this? No — schedule and workflow_dispatch only run on the default branch context.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated

  gate:
    if: >-

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone.
